verdict.headline: Iran exits Hormuz talks, sending oil above $90 and 30-year yields to a 19-year high
verdict.label: STEP ASIDE — 3 of 4 regime triggers breached: 30Y 5.31% (first close above 5.28% gate, 19-year high); Brent $91.50 and WTI $85.50 both above oil thresholds; BTC $64,289 AH holds above $62K gate. VIX +6.60% to 15.19 on the session — confirming the vol reprice the dual-breach warranted. MSFT −3.17%, META −3.63%, RDDT −7.14% (inclusion day). FOMC Minutes Wednesday 2pm ET; Walmart Thursday; NVDA Aug 26
verdict.rationale_short: Iran ruled out any Hormuz MOU extension and Brent surpassed $90; the 30Y closed at 5.31%, the first breach of the 5.28% regime trigger at a 19-year high. VIX moved decisively higher (+6.60% to 15.19) confirming the session's macro stress was real. MSFT and META each fell more than 3% on reinforcing headwinds — a Morgan Stanley hyperscaler creditworthiness note and a 30-state AG trial — while RDDT closed −7.14% as insider Form 144 supply overwhelmed the S&P 500 inclusion auction. BTC recovered from a $63,020 intraday low to $64,289 AH, holding the $62K gate by a $2,289 buffer. The level that changes this read: SPX closes above 7,800 on two consecutive sessions with the 30Y back below 5.25%.

trade_setups.thesis: The 30Y closed at 5.31%, the first breach of the 5.28% trigger and the highest yield in 19 years. FOMC Minutes Wednesday (July 28–29 meeting, three hawkish dissenters) could extend the move toward 5.40% — a level historically associated with broad P/E compression in long-duration tech — if the dissenters' rationale was fiscal sustainability rather than CPI persistence.
trade_setups.entry: 5.28% was the trigger (now breached); 5.40% is the next technically meaningful level; 5.20–5.25% is retracement support if Minutes reveal isolated dissenters on inflation.
trade_setups.invalidation: 30Y retraces below 5.25% on two sessions after FOMC Minutes; September hike odds fall below 25%.

trade_setups.thesis: Both fell 3%+ on the same session with distinct catalysts (hyperscaler creditworthiness note; AG trial), together representing a simultaneous re-rating of AI infrastructure spending cost (MSFT) and AI application profitability (META). NVDA's August 26 print is the next test of whether the re-rating extends to the infrastructure enabler.

trade_setups.invalidation: Either name recovers above today's close within 2 sessions on no new catalyst, indicating the specific drivers were already absorbed.

trade_setups.thesis: RDDT closed at ~$165.38 on its S&P 500 inclusion day — below the $177 post-mechanics threshold. The question is whether $158 (pre-announcement close) holds as support or whether the full reversal of the inclusion pop is now underway. Two closes below $158 on Aug 18–19 would confirm the advertising-durability question was not answered by the passive mechanics.
trade_setups.entry: $158 is the pre-announcement reference; $165 is current close; $177 is the level that would indicate fundamental demand present.
trade_setups.invalidation: Two consecutive closes above $177 on Aug 18–19 confirm advertising-durability demand met the passive bid.

bear_case: Three of four regime indicators breached simultaneously — 30Y at 5.31% (19-year high), Brent at $91.50, WTI at $85.50 — while VIX repriced +6.60% to 15.19, confirming the session's macro stress was not a non-event. Unlike Friday's vol compression, Monday's VIX move is consistent with a genuine risk-off tone. The setup into Tuesday: Walmart earnings and Home Depot (consumer resilience check), FOMC Minutes Wednesday 2pm ET (three hawkish dissenters from the July 28–29 meeting), Flash PMI Friday. Brent retracing below $89 on interim Hormuz progress and the 30Y compressing below 5.25% on dovish Minutes would reverse all three regime breaches simultaneously. Credit spreads have not widened materially and SPX avoided a full-percent decline, which keeps this STEP ASIDE rather than BEARISH. NVDA Aug 26 remains the single most important event for the AI tape heading into Jackson Hole.
